lines.text: The dam at Vajont did not fail.
The dam was a wall of concrete two hundred and sixty-two metres high.
The river below it ran down to the town of Longarone.
But the mountainside above the reservoir was already creeping.
Inside it a slab of rock rested on a weak bed of clay.
Water from the reservoir soaked into that clay until the bed let go.
On the ninth of October the slab slid into the lake in forty-five seconds.
Two hundred and seventy million cubic metres of rock took the reservoir's place.
The lake had nowhere to go but over the crest of the dam.
Minutes later it reached the town of Longarone, and two thousand people died.
The dam is still standing, and they built the wrong thing correctly.
